title: Adaptive entry safeguards and pin-playbook for catalog onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to onboard community/open model weights into the catalog to expand coverage and lower unit cost for customers. Recent incidents showed subtle runtime incompatibilities (KV-cache mismatches, attention kernel fallbacks) after unpinned model variants were promoted. This ticket defines a pragmatic, adaptive entry-safeguard and pin-playbook to clarify when to require hard pins, when to allow soft (gradual) pins, and what compatibility metadata the runtime and console must surface so downstream teams can make safe rollout decisions.

Goals: Provide deterministic acceptance criteria for new open-model entries; reduce emergency rollbacks by >80%; provide clear runtime compatibility signals in catalog UI and API; enable staged rollouts with automated fallback.

Scope: Requirements for model intake and acceptance gating (metadata schema, runtime checks, eval harness integration), the pin decision matrix (hard pin, soft pin, no pin), rollout policy templates (canary percentages, time windows), monitoring and automated fallback rules.

Out of scope: Changes to model training pipelines, major runtime kernel rewrites, enterprise-only contractual SLA changes (handled by Dedicated/Private tracks).

Design constraints and principles: prioritize safety-first for host customers; prefer lightweight instrumentation over blocking blocks; allow experimental variants in a discovery channel with stricter telemetry and shorter TTLs. Pin decisions must be reversible and observable.

Acceptance criteria (high level): see acceptance_criteria field.

Implementation notes: 1) Add three new catalog metadata keys: runtime_compat_level (LOW|MED|HIGH), expected_kv_semantics (strict|lenient|unknown), recommended_pin (hard|soft|none). 2) Intake UI must require a short rationale and source provenance link for unpinned variants. 3) Runtime must check model signature at first warmup request and emit a compat_verification event to observability. 4) Console should surface a single-line compatibility summary and an impact score (0-100) derived from evals + runtime probes. 5) Create a small canary policy template: 1% traffic for 24h, evaluate latency/error/regression delta; escalate or expand.

Rollout plan: Phase 1 (dev): schema + runtime probe (2 sprints). Phase 2 (beta): UI surfaces + canary template + one pilot community model (1 sprint). Phase 3 (GA): default enforcement for public catalog entries + docs and migration guide (2 sprints).

Monitoring and alerting: New dashboard tab 'compat-entry' with the following charts: compat_verification failures, rolling latency delta per model, quality regression alerts based on eval score. Define automated fallback: if latency p95 increases >50ms AND error rate >0.5% for 30min, route to pinned fallback variant or previous model.

Rollback and emergency actions: Provide a single-click revert in Console to pin previous stable variant and drain canary. Add a runbook in Confluence with triage checklist.

Open questions: 1) How strict should 'expected_kv_semantics' checks be for legacy models? 2) Should community model entries be allowed in the main catalog without a 'soft pin' default? 3) How to weight eval score vs runtime probe when computing impact score?

Success metrics: reduction in post-onboard rollback incidents by 80% within 3 months of GA; new-model rollout mean time to detect regressions < 20 minutes; catalog entries with compat metadata coverage 95%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Catalog metadata schema added and validated: runtime_compat_level, expected_kv_semantics, recommended_pin; intake rejects missing required fields for public entries.
2) Runtime emits compat_verification event on first warmup and on model version change; observability captures these events and they appear in the 'compat-entry' dashboard.
3) Console shows compatibility summary and impact score for each model entry; the UI displays recommended_pin prominently and links to the intake rationale.
4) Canary rollout template implemented: supports % traffic, duration window, automatic evaluation of latency/error/quality deltas, and failsafe fallback action.
5) Pilot complete: onboard one community model using the playbook, run 48h canary, and document results; post-pilot report approved by eng + PM + security.
6) Migration guide and runbook published in Confluence; at least two SRE/Eng reviewers + one security reviewer have signed off.
7) Automated alerting thresholds configured so that any new-model rollout triggers a paging alert if the defined fallback conditions are met.
8) Post-GA measurement plan instrumented: dashboards show rollback incidents and detection latency; initial 30-day baseline captured.
9) Documentation: intake form help text, playbook steps, and decision matrix published and linked from Console help.
10) Security review completed and any required mitigations tracked as child issues.
